name: Flutterfly Dust

faq.answer: The resident says the dust has practical household uses, but keeps its purpose vague, calling it general stuff and things.
faq.q: What is flutterfly dust used for?

faq.answer: Giant flutterflies roam the outer fields near the local orchard, especially across the Gustberry Lowlands. Bandits nearby make gathering there dangerous for anyone alone.
Flutterflies are usually docile and flee when disturbed. Some defend themselves when swatted or provoked, then release their wing dust.
A Flutterfly Swatter delivers a firm blow to the oversized insects. As they react, some shake their rumps and scatter piles of wing dust for gathering.
The resident lives alone and cannot easily leave the homestead to gather the dust. Bandits across the surrounding lowlands make a trip far into the fields too dangerous.
faq.q: Why does the resident need someone else to gather the dust?

faq.answer: The resident refuses to explain the dust's household use and waves off questions with talk of things and stuff. Its purpose remains unexplained.
faq.q: Why is the resident evasive about the dust's true purpose?

sections.body: Giant flutterflies drift through the outer fields and orchards of the Gustberry Lowlands. Their wings shed fine dust, and you can gather it in bulk. Nearby homesteaders want the powder for practical household needs. Yet the insects remain wild.
sections.title: The Giants of Gustberry

sections.body: A Flutterfly Swatter brings dust down with a blunt strike. Most flutterflies panic, take to the air, and shake loose piles of powder. Some turn and strike back when provoked. Usually, they are docile.
sections.title: Swatters and Shakes

sections.body: The dust is messy to gather and clings to clothing and gear for weeks. The homesteader eagerly awaits its delivery, since bandits make solo trips into the fields too dangerous. Ask what the powder is for, and the resident offers only vague words about general stuff and things.
sections.title: Unspoken Applications

summary: In the Gustberry Lowlands, Flutterfly Dust draws a homesteader's interest. Travelers gather it from giant flutterflies while bandits threaten anyone who ventures alone into the fields.
